gates.reason: Narrative performance audit; it does not define authentication, filesystem writes, egress, client rendering, command execution, Kubernetes, container, TLS, secret, or supply-chain behavior.

Recommendation and calculation claims identify the dated snapshot, denominators, detector families, provenance requirements, confidence limits, non-overlap rules, and reproducibility commands; observational ceilings are explicitly separated from realized savings.

The document directly addresses performance and supplies bounded detector contracts, non-overlapping clock accounting, causal probes, acceptance gates, budgets/countermetrics, and explicit deferrals where latency evidence is unavailable.

The only governed egress surface is identified as an explicit opt-in request for first-party response headers; local Claude/Codex artifacts remain identified as local acquisition sources, and the audit states that prompts, outputs, credentials, and secret values were not read into the report.

Signal claims cite concrete artifact fields and parser owners, distinguish native from derived measurements, carry confidence and semantic caveats, require structured observation provenance, preserve stale/unsupported states, and forbid substituting missing values with zero.

The inventory defines the performance probes and measurement contract for turn time, round trips, TTFT, token counters, and runway, including coverage, freshness, semantics versions, and strict capability gating; no unprobed performance surface is introduced.
